answer: Accounts are grouped by the hour they joined, stamped by a public beacon so entry cannot be backdated, and all attestations from one hourly cohort count as a single vote. 1,000 sybils made in one hour get 1 vote; 1,000 votes need 1,000 distinct hours (~42 days) of staked, aging accounts. Weight climbs a terrace of steps with cohort age. Cohorts that always vote alike are slashed. Colluders sharing an hour share one vote, and spreading out only widens the canyon of time each must fund alone. Honest users join at scattered times and lose nothing.
